decisions.reason: As a core-adjacent wafer innovation, it still fits the firm's process and customer base and is relatively cheap to keep available, but after several years its specialized through-contact niche leaves enough unresolved demand risk to make withdrawal a real possibility.

The copper interposer glass wafer is a strategic flagship closely aligned with the firm's direction toward advanced packaging wafers, so its option value remains high and the firm should keep it while market adoption in semiconductor applications matures.
The off-the-shelf wafer brand is close to the established offer, spreads development risk across several standard models, and likely has low incremental carrying cost, so it is worth keeping open.

Glass-based circuit boards are comparatively distant from the firm's narrow core business, require different market development and commitment, and with no clear evidence of traction the option value no longer justifies tying up resources.
